title: Testing Associative Creativity in Humans and Multimodal LLMs with Difficult-to-Name Visual Stimuli
abstract: arXiv:2610.27894v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We investigate associative creativity in descriptions of abstract visual stimuli by humans and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). While conceptual association is central to human communication, it remains unclear how humans and models adapt when visual stimuli become increasingly difficult to map onto familiar semantic concepts. We evaluate several state-of-the-art MLLMs and human participants along two dimensions of creativity, originality and effectiveness, using two datasets with controlled manipulations of difficulty. SilCC varies naming difficulty through progressively more complex combinations of abstract shapes, and PixCC varies difficulty through increasing levels of random visual noise. Results show that humans produce more diverse associative descriptions than MLLMs, including greater semantic distance, higher entropy, and more novel expressions relative to reference lexica. As difficulty increases, effectiveness decline

translated_title: 用难以命名的视觉刺激测试人类和多模态大语言模型的联想创造力
translated_abstract: 我们研究了人类和多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在描述抽象视觉刺激时的联想创造力。虽然概念联想是人类交流的核心，但当视觉刺激越来越难以映射到熟悉的语义概念时，人类和模型如何适应仍不清楚。我们使用两个具有受控难度操纵的数据集，从原创性和有效性这两个创造力维度评估了多个最先进的多模态大语言模型和人类参与者。SilCC通过逐渐更复杂的抽象形状组合来改变命名难度，PixCC则通过增加随机视觉噪声水平来改变难度。结果表明，人类比多模态大语言模型产生更多样化的联想描述，包括相对于参考词库具有更大的语义距离、更高的熵以及更多新颖的表达。随着难度增加，有效性下降。
tldr: 该研究通过SilCC和PixCC两个可控难度数据集评估人类与多模态大语言模型对难以命名的抽象视觉刺激的联想创造力，发现人类的联想描述更多样、更新颖、语义距离更大，而模型的有效性随难度增加而下降。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates associative creativity of humans and multimodal LLMs on difficult-to-name visual stimuli using two difficulty-controlled datasets (SilCC and PixCC), finding that humans produce more diverse, novel, and semantically distant descriptions than MLLMs, whose effectiveness declines as difficulty increases.
